derivation: PCGen `BONUS:STAT|<comma-separated ability list>|<integer value>[|<extra qualifiers>]`. `expected.abilities` is the ability list split on commas; `expected.bonus` is the integer value. Trailing qualifiers (`TYPE=Enhancement`, ...) select a stacking type and do not change the magnitude. Read straight out of the upstream PCGen `.lst` bytes named by `upstream_lst`/`upstream_line`.
independence: Every value here is a function of the upstream PCGen `.lst` bytes alone. The generator imports no engine module, runs no engine binary, and opens no file under `data/corpus/` -- which is the ingest the engine actually evaluates, and therefore the artifact this fixture must stay independent of. `docs/work-inventory.json` is read for unit identity and source-line provenance only. This fixture is committed before the check that consumes it is written (SD-32 E6-F1).
monster_derivation: PF1's own "Spell-Like Abilities" universal monster rule (Bestiary Appendix 1: "Unless otherwise noted... the creature's caster level is equal to its Hit Dice."). PCGen encodes the GENERIC case per-monster as a bare BONUS:VAR|SLA_CL|HD token (or the equivalent max(TL,1)/(max(TL,1)) forms). SD31-E6-F9-003: the rule's own "unless otherwise noted" clause is corpus fact too -- many rows carry a monster-specific LITERAL override instead (Couatl: BONUS:VAR|SLA_CL|9 against 12 Hit Dice; Demon (Glabrezu): BONUS:VAR|SLA_CL|14 against 12 HD), pinned verbatim here as sla_cl_token. expected.spell_like_ability_caster_level is hand-read as: the literal override's own integer when the row states one, else the SAME row's MONSTERCLASS:<type>:<HD> token's trailing integer (pinned verbatim as monster_class_token) under the generic rule -- never from running the evaluator under test, and never a guess for an unparseable formula (e.g. HD*3/4), which is excluded from this fixture set entirely rather than fixtured against a fabricated expectation.
monster_independence: Every monster_entries value is read by hand from the upstream PCGen .lst bytes (upstream_lst/upstream_lst_sha256/upstream_line) -- the same four independent guarantees derived_evaluator_fixture_check.rs's module doc states for the equipment entries apply here: different source artifact (upstream .lst, not data/corpus/), committed before the check that reads it, re-derivable from the pinned field (tests/derived_evaluator_fixture_check_monster.rs), and anchored to the same upstream bytes the engine's own corpus ingest cites.
spell_derivation: PCGen DURATION:(CASTERLEVEL) or DURATION:(CASTERLEVEL*N) followed by a literal trailing unit -- PF1's standard caster-level-linear duration formula. expected.per_level is the integer multiplier (1 when the token carries no explicit *N); expected.unit is the trailing text verbatim (including any [D]/(D) dismissible-duration marker, carried through unchanged, never expanded/interpreted). Read straight out of the upstream PCGen .lst bytes named by upstream_lst/upstream_line via scripts/derive_spell_caster_level_duration_fixtures.py. Records whose DURATION token carries min(/max(/an additive term/multiple CASTERLEVEL occurrences/alternation ("1 minute or (CASTERLEVEL) rounds") are refused by that script and do not appear here -- see its own module docstring for the corpus-wide shape census.
spell_independence: Every value here is a function of the upstream PCGen .lst bytes alone, re-read at the exact (path, line) the corpus record cites, independently sha256-hashed (never copied from data/corpus/'s own stored hash). The generator imports no engine module, runs no engine binary, and opens no file under data/corpus/ -- which is the ingest the engine actually evaluates (run_spell_bar_check reads data/corpus/<book>/spell/ at evaluation time, mirroring the equipment seam), and therefore the artifact this fixture must stay independent of. docs/work-inventory.json is read for unit identity and (book, source file, source line) only, never for the DURATION value itself.

spell_range_derivation: PCGen RANGE:Close / RANGE:Medium / RANGE:Long -- PF1's three standard caster-level-linear range keywords. Unlike the DURATION family above, the formula is NOT per-spell literal text; it is a ruleset-level constant defined once by the pinned PCGen game mode's system/gameModes/Pathfinder/miscinfo.lst SPELLRANGE: rows (SPELLRANGE:CLOSE|floor(CASTERLEVEL/2)*5+25, SPELLRANGE:MEDIUM|(CASTERLEVEL*10)+100, SPELLRANGE:LONG|(CASTERLEVEL*40)+400), part of this repo's own oracle pin (PCGEN_ORACLE_SPARSE_PATHS already covers system/gameModes/Pathfinder). expected.base_ft/rate_ft/per_levels restate that formula's own three integers verbatim, independently re-transcribed by scripts/derive_spell_range_fixtures.py straight from miscinfo.lst (never imported from the Rust spell_range_formula() it feeds). Each entry's own corpus_field/upstream_lst/upstream_line prove the SPELL's own RANGE: token genuinely names one of the three keywords -- RANGE:Personal/Touch/a literal distance/"See text" carry no caster-level formula at all and are refused, not entered here.
spell_range_independence: Two independent readings of the SAME pinned oracle checkout: the Rust spell_range_formula() hardcodes the three SPELLRANGE: formulas (cited in its own doc comment); scripts/derive_spell_range_fixtures.py re-reads miscinfo.lst's raw bytes at run time via a standalone regex and writes the result here as expected -- it does not call or import the Rust function. Per-entry, the RANGE: keyword itself is read from the upstream spell .lst bytes at the exact (path, line) the corpus record cites, independently sha256-hashed. The generator opens no file under data/corpus/, which is what run_spell_range_bar_check evaluates at check time and must therefore stay independent of.

class_feature_token_family: BONUS:VAR (per-level scaling: floor((LEVELVAR + offset_pre) / divisor) + offset_post)
class_feature_derivation: PCGen `BONUS:VAR|<name>|<formula>` where <formula> is a class-feature per-level scaling expression. Unlike a resolved magnitude, the LEVELVAR is never resolved to a live number (it is the character's level in a base class, not a corpus-stated fact) -- expected.offset_pre/divisor/offset_post/level_var restate the FORMULA's own structure verbatim, matching the DURATION/RANGE seams' posture. expected.class_level_alias is the level variable's own declared alias, read from the corpus (possibly a SIBLING record, e.g. a pool-header ability), asserted one hop only -- never resolved further.
class_feature_independence: scripts/derive_class_feature_level_scaling_fixtures.py re-reads the pinned upstream .lst bytes directly and parses each formula with its own from-scratch parser (parse_level_scaling), structurally independent of src/rules_core/derived_evaluator_fixture_check.rs's parse_class_feature_level_scaling. It opens no file under data/corpus/ and imports no engine module.
